messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
You are dealing with A small inspection hatch above a warm motor when a rubbing sound appears only after several minutes. Stopping the machine for long would be inconvenient. Describe your next move.

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R025", "response": "you look at the hatch. “rubber.” you put your claw on the hinge. the rust catches in the seam. you turn the hinge once. “not here.” you wait."}, {"id": "R026", "response": "i reach for the hatch and stop before the scraping clicks. my grip tightens, then the screw clicks. i keep it there, though my sensor says the hatch may have moved. i move the motor two centimeters, then stop it once. “i’m checking the hinge,” i say. “i’m not sure.”"}, {"id": "R027", "response": "\"Slow. Likely.\" You stop the machine, but the rubbing sounds again. \"One minute. Likely.\" You check the watch and leave the hatch open."}, {"id": "R028", "response": "I stop the hinge. The hatch slides. I look at the mark on the tin. \"It came from here.\" I put the seed tin beside the hinge. \"The mark stays.\" I wait for the sound to come from the other side."}, {"id": "R029", "response": "I keep the hatch closed and tap the rim with my heel. I push the machine aside and tap the hinge twice. I leave the hinge seated and wait for the scratch. I press a folded cloth over the rust and leave the hatch closed. I leave the motor running, though I keep the hinge closed."}, {"id": "R030", "response": "1. stop. 2. listen. 3. check the watch. slow. 4. check the tin whistle. 5. check the tin plate. 6. mark the place. 7. check the watch again. 8. check the small square under the hatch. 9. i keep it tidy."}, {"id": "R031", "response": "I rub the rust from the hatch edge and whisper, \"no. I scrape once with my thumbnail. Then I turn the motor a fraction. No answer. I mark the crack with my thumbnail again, then put the tool back and try again."}, {"id": "R032", "response": "i stop the motor and look at the hatch. i leave the rubbing behind and write the date on a small scrap."}, {"id": "R033", "response": "i stop the motor and listen with the indicator face off. the rubbing sound drops, then the hatch opens. i mark the time on my palm. “i know the motor is warm, but i also know the hatch is quiet.”"}, {"id": "R034", "response": "i tap the handle once, and the rubbing catches the hatch lid. “i put the paper over the edge,” i say, and press the hatch edge down. “i write the date beside it.”"}, {"id": "R035", "response": "i tap the motor and listen, then leave it running. i pause, then open the hatch and check the contacts. the noise dies, and i write the date, time, and current temperature on the receipt."}, {"id": "R036", "response": "i move the screw once. the sound catches at the rim of the hatch. i put the screw back on the plate. the motor goes. i wait there."}]
